Q: Automatically generate <a> tag from <img> tag A:

पृष्ठभूमि (Background): एक गहरी, काली/ग्रे ग्रेफिटी वाली दीवार, जैसे स्कूल की दीवार.

बाईं ओर: आपका पसंदीदा "भयानक भालू" (image_4.png से) बना हुआ है, लेकिन इसे थोड़ा 'टेक्निकल' और 'इलेक्ट्रिक' वाइब दी गई है.

बीच में: आपका चैनल नाम "THE NEXT BACKBENCHER" को बोल्ड, टेढ़े-मेढ़े और रफ फोंट में लिखा गया है (जैसे किसी ने स्प्रे पेंट से लिखा हो).

दाईं ओर: एक टूटा हुआ, पुराना डेस्क और उसके पास एक "उल्टा चश्मा" बना हो, जो 'फन' और 'शरारत' को दर्शाता है.

निचले हिस्से में: "यहाँ ज्ञान नहीं, जुगाड़ मिलता है! 😎" - यह आपकी टैगलाइन होगी.

डिज़ाइन कॉन्सेप्ट 2: 'गेमिंग बैकबेंचर' (The Gaming Backbencher)

अगर आप गेमिंग या टेक्नोलॉजी से जुड़ा कंटेंट बनाने वाले हैं, तो यह डिज़ाइन आपको बहुत पसंद आएगा.

पृष्ठभूमि (Background): एक गहरा, फ्यूचरिस्टिक साइबर-ग्रे बैकग्राउंड, जैसे image_4.png के कंप्यूटर स्क्रीन पर है, लेकिन थोड़ा अधिक सूक्ष्म.

बीच में: आपका पसंदीदा "भयानक भालू" (image_4.png) को सबसे बड़ा और केंद्रीय हिस्सा बनाया गया है.

भालू के ऊपर: "THE NEXT" को एक साफ, आधुनिक और तकनीकी फोंट में लिखा गया है.

भालू के नीचे: "BACKBENCHER" को एक बड़े, भारी और मिलिट्री-स्टाइल फोंट में लिखा गया है.

दाईं ओर: एक गेमिंग कंसोल और एक कीबोर्ड का आइकन बना हुआ है.

निचले हिस्से में: "कंट्रोलर से क्लास तक - सब यहाँ! 🎮"

डिज़ाइन कॉन्सेप्ट 3: 'अजीब कला' (The Anti-Design)

यह सबसे अलग और रचनात्मक होगा. यह नियमों को मानने से इनकार करता है, बिल्कुल एक बैकबेंचर की तरह.

पृष्ठभूमि (Background): एक चमकीला पीला (केले का रंग) और गहरा काला बैकग्राउंड, जिसमें कुछ पॉप-अप रंगों (जैसे लाल और हरा) का मिश्रण है.

बीच में: "THE NEXT" को बहुत सीधा और साफ-सुथरा लिखा गया है, जबकि "BACKBENCHER" को एकदम अजीब, बेमेल और टूटे-फूटे अक्षरों में लिखा गया है (जैसे नियमों को तोड़ा गया हो).

अक्षरों के बीच में: एक छोटा सा, पिक्सेलेटेड (Pixelated) केला (Nano Banana) और आपका पसंदीदा "भयानक भालू" (image_4.png) का एक सूक्ष्म, लाइन-आर्ट संस्करण.

Q: Efficient Spark Strategy for Joining 1.5M Accounts Across Two Systems of Record A:

Option 3 is actually a decent idea in concept, but there's a catch with how PySpark handles connections. Volatile tables in Teradata are tied to a single session — the moment that session closes, the table is gone. The problem is PySpark doesn't work with a single connection; it spins up multiple JDBC connections across tasks and partitions, so a volatile table created in one connection simply won't exist in another. That makes it unreliable for this use case.

A cleaner alternative would be to use a Teradata Global Temporary Table (GTT) instead — these aren't session-bound the same way, so multiple connections can work with them. Another option worth exploring is a dedicated staging table in SOR-B. I know the concern was about writing to SOR-B, but that's likely aimed at production tables — a separate staging area is a different conversation and might be acceptable if you bring it back to the table with that distinction clearly made.

Q: Python code to create link based on the title A:

You probably don't want to reinvent the wheel, so, you might want to use Django's slugify filter. Of course, you don't need to use Django to use it, and you could try and have a look at the source code and just get what you want so you don't have to have the whole Django packages installed to make this work.

Here's what you'll get:

>>> from django.template.defaultfilters import slugify
>>> slugify("""Global across "Modules" ?""")
u'global-across-modules'
>>>

Note that slugs are meant to be used in URLs in Django, so they're URL safe.

Q: One aync lock call or multiple async lock calls, what is better and safer in Python? A:

One async lock call is safer. Your code is not safe.

Btw, it is meaningless to allow concurrency in the rate limiter of a user. It should be an atomic action. It is only meaningful to have concurrency in the part of the business logic of the request. (In case you are trying to make your server slightly faster by sacrificing the strictness of the limit, here's a reminder that releasing and acquiring a lock costs overhead too.)

Your case:

You have four steps which call the same lock:

  • uid_requests.reset_day_limit()
  • uid_requests.exited_day_limit()
  • uid_requests.rate_limited()
  • uid_requests.add_reuqest()

if many requests were sent at the same time, at the period when no one has reached the uid_requests.add_reuqest() step, uid_requests.exited_day_limit() and uid_requests.rate_limited doesn't limit any requests.

Fix:

  1. RequestsData.on_request:
async def on_request(self) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
    async with self._async_lock:
        current_time_seconds = self.get_now_seconds()

        # check and reset total requests start time as current time seconds
        if self.total_requests_start_time is not None:
            if current_time_seconds - self.total_requests_start_time > self.day_len_seconds:
                self.total_requests_start_time = current_time_seconds
                self.total_requests = 0

        # check exited day limit
        if self.total_requests >= self.max_requests_per_day:
            if self.just_limit_exited:
                self.just_limit_exited = False
                return (True, False)
            return (False, False)

        # check rate limited by last time
        if self.last_time is not None and current_time_seconds - self.last_time < self.seconds_interval:
            if self.just_limit_exited:
                self.just_limit_exited = False
                return (True, False)
            return (False, False)

        # add request with last time as now
        self.last_time = current_time_seconds
        self.just_limit_exited = True
        self.total_requests += 1

        return (False, True)
  1. RateLimiter.on_request
async def on_request(self, uid: int) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
    uid_requests: RequestsData = self.requsts[uid]
    return await uid_requests.on_request()

Other problems:

  • (fixed) if self.total_requests >= self.max_requests_per_day - 1: is wrong. No need - 1.
  • (not fixed) total_requests_start_time is never initialized. Not sure how u want it to work because you explicity ignored it in your code. (if self.total_requests_start_time is None: return True)
  • (not fixed) get_now_seconds is decorated with @classmethod but takes self. Better to use cls.

Q: problem with background legend color of a ggplot when I add a loess smooth with visible SE band A:

I noticed that you have the same code twice both use se = FALSE. The issue appears when se = TRUE.

When se = TRUE, geom_smooth() adds confidence band (a ribbon), which in the end introduces a fill aesthetic into the legend. That fill seems to override your white legend background.

You can fix it by removing the fill from the legend using override.aes:

example

ggplot(dcomb, aes(x = DatHr, y = Radon, colour = endroit)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 0.2, se = TRUE) +
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(fill = NA)
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.8, 0.95),
    legend.justification.inside = c("center", "top"),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)
  )
